findings.title: Human naming raises a label without granting warrant
findings.claim: Humanly assigned names can raise an object's social designation, while the focus's denied descent from Allah leaves that designation without evidentiary or governing authority.
findings.mechanism: The focus places names and naming under human and ancestral agency, then places descended authorization and sultan under negation; the exact 53:23 and 7:71 parallels repeat that sequence, allowing naming, lineage, divine delivery, proof, and authority to contact one another.
findings.reader_payoff: A name becomes visible as a socially elevated designation whose inherited repetition can look authoritative while remaining only a label until warrant is supplied.
findings.containment: The reading adds pressure to the naming critique and keeps ordinary naming intact. It does not erase reference, claim every human designation is false, or turn the parallel's absent warrant into a general statement about all authority.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication and exact supplied target Arabic establish the carrier-trigger relation; the legacy reader-walk records corroborate the same bounded reading without serving as independent proof.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 53:23 target repeats names and the human act of assigning them before the absent sultan clause.
branch_activations.activation: The parallel places the focus's naming word inside the same contrast between a label and a warrant-bearing claim.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The named objects remain identifiable names, while their social designation is exposed as a claim that still needs authority.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make every ordinary name a false authority or replace the focus's plain reference to named objects.

findings.title: Judgment redirects repeated practice into an upright course
findings.claim: The sole judgment and commanded exclusive worship can redirect habitual social allegiance into a stable, upright order.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins al-hukm, the command to worship, al-din, and al-qayyim; supplied parallels show judgment restraining or deciding, command directing worship, din naming an obedience-and-rules system, and qayyim naming a straight order.
findings.reader_payoff: Exclusive worship becomes perceptible as an ordering act that reaches repeated communal practice, not only as a private label for devotion.
findings.containment: The finding adds the effect of the focus's judgment and command on practice while preserving the plain religious sense. It does not turn this ayah into a general political theory or replace its direct claim that worship belongs to Allah alone.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication supplies the integrated relation and the exact target Arabic supplies distinct returns for judgment, command, din, and uprightness; the legacy walk is corroborative and remains qualified by provenance.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Sole judgment gathers worship away from competing directions and checks the practice that would keep returning to them.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation retains the focus's judgment claim and does not reduce all judgment to physical restraint.

findings.title: Sultan can also mark coercive power
findings.claim: The focus's denied sultan can also be heard as denied coercive power: a named claim or invitation has no force to compel.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries sultan in the no-warrant clause, while the exact 14:22 target distinguishes possessed sultan from a mere invitation that people accept; the same focus term therefore touches power to compel as a separate authority facet.
findings.reader_payoff: The denial reaches beyond lack of proof to the practical question of whether a label can bend anyone's action by force.
findings.containment: This adds the coercive-power facet alongside the proof and governing-authority facets already grounded in the naming contrast. It does not replace them or claim that every persuasive invitation is coercion.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic and accepted focus branch supply a real contact, while the connection's prior retrieval label is not treated as source trust and target morphology is absent.

branch_activations.boundary: This keeps the proof and authority readings live and does not claim that every name lacks every kind of influence.

findings.title: Din opens an accountability horizon

findings.containment: The accountability horizon deepens the focus's din without replacing its plain religious-order reading. The supplied 51:6 note explicitly frames the focus phrase as ordered practice rather than due consequence, so both contacts remain live and this addition stays qualified.

epistemic.reason: Fatiha 1:4 supplies an exact target return to din and 51:6 supplies live counter-evidence; target morphology is absent and neither connection prior label is treated as a decision.

findings.containment: The added recognition facet preserves the plain statement that most people do not know. It does not turn every knowledge use into a physical sign or claim that the focus's closing has only one kind of ignorance.

epistemic.reason: The exact targets supply guidance and knowledge contacts through the focus verb, but the focus branch is qualified and the target morphology is not supplied.
